children: Berenberg, which reiterated its 'buy' rating on the stock, argued that the Discoverie's quality‑compounder model continues to offer upside and said the firm's H1 trading update confirmed a clear acceleration in organic growth, with the group expecting 10% year‑on‑year organic growth for the half.

Organic orders rose 22%, marking more than a year of consecutive order book build and underpinning future delivery. Berenberg also raised its adjusted earnings per share forecasts by 2% to 3% across the forecast period.

Momentum was broad‑based, led by Discoverie's magnetics and controls unit, which grew 13% organically, while sensing and connectivity was now positioned to accelerate as supply lead times normalise and tougher comparators fall away. Orders increased 25% in M&C and 18% in S&C, producing a book‑to‑bill ratio of 1.12.

Overall sales rose 13% at constant currency, supported by recent acquisitions, while net debt-to-underkying earnings stood at 1.6x at the end of September, rising to around 1.8x post‑acquisition, which Berenberg said still leaves roughly £35m of short‑term M&A capacity.

Berenberg added that DiscoverIE's long‑term compounding potential remains underappreciated, with management's 17% FY30 EBIT margin target and the benefits of the 3Gmetalworx deal not yet reflected in forecasts, offering a supportive backdrop for shareholder returns. Regulatory approval for the firm's acquisition of 3Gmetalworx was said to be progressing, with completion expected shortly
Reporting by Iain Gilbert at Sharecast.com
